adds.rationale: Robotics — the profile's #2-ranked next wave — showed concrete Q4 2024 buildup signals (major corporate capital commitment, government-backed R&D, new commercial humanoid product launches) with zero current watchlist exposure, so a diversified robotics ETF fills the gap without single-name concentration risk.

news_evidence.summary: Samsung Electronics announced it will raise its stake in Rainbow Robotics to 35% for roughly $181M, becoming the humanoid robot maker's largest shareholder and creating a Future Robotics Office.
ROBOTIS (South Korea) announced a partnership with MIT to develop 'Physical AI' under a government-backed international R&D project worth up to 10 billion won.

removes.rationale: IonQ's 2024 rally reversed sharply into year-end even as losses persisted on thin revenue, and Google's in-house Willow chip breakthrough signals a well-capitalized hyperscaler competitor racing into quantum hardware — a peak-enthusiasm-plus-competition signal that argues for trimming the sole quantum slot in favor of the more clearly buildup-stage robotics wave.

news_evidence.summary: IonQ was up 97% YTD in mid-October 2024, but that gain had collapsed to just 8% YTD by December 29, 2024, even after beating Q3 revenue guidance with a $52.5M net loss.
Google Quantum AI announced its Willow chip, achieving below-threshold quantum error correction — a large, well-funded hyperscaler advancing its own in-house quantum hardware.

rationale_overall: Net effect is a one-for-one swap that re-balances the watchlist toward the profile's own wave-priority ordering: robotics (ranked #2) enters via a diversified ETF on the back of concrete Q4 2024 buildup evidence (Samsung's $181M controlling stake in Rainbow Robotics, government-backed ROBOTIS-MIT R&D), while IonQ (the sole quantum holding, ranked #3) is trimmed after its 2024 surge visibly cooled into year-end and Google's Willow chip raised the competitive bar for quantum pure-plays. AI (MSFT, NVDA), rockets (RKLB — record backlog and revenue growth per Q3 2024), and nuclear (OKLO — advancing its Groves Isotope Test Reactor through DOE review) are all left intact as their in-window news continued to support the buildup/surge thesis.
